name: K92 Mining
inflation_thesis: Sells unhedged USD gold (plus copper) against a local PNG cost base that rises more slowly than gold, so an inflation-driven gold rally goes almost straight to margin. The Stage 3 plant roughly triples throughput, so ounces and price per ounce rise together.
key_risks: Ramp-up execution worries (Q2-26 13% EPS miss) and PNG sovereign/security risk.
notes: Price is the US OTC line (KNTNF) so it matches USD EPS. FY2/FY3 from Simply Wall St net income / ~242m shares (Mar-26, pre-selloff). Scotiabank FY27 EPS $2.48. BMO target C$40, RBC C$45.

name: Vista Energy
inflation_thesis: Sells crude at Brent-linked, USD export-parity prices while much of its cost base is in Argentine pesos, so hot US inflation that lifts USD oil prices drops straight to margins. Production is growing ~30%+ a year (Q2-26 output +32% y/y, revenue +102% after the La Amarga Chica deal), so price and volume compound, and its long-life shale reserves are a hard asset.
key_risks: Argentine political, FX and capital-control risk; pipeline/export bottlenecks out of Vaca Muerta.
notes: FY0 = 2025 adjusted EPS $3.30 (reported $7.0 included a one-off acquisition gain). Revenue consensus not found. 100% of analysts rate Buy; avg target ~$90.

name: Eldorado Gold
inflation_thesis: Mostly unhedged USD gold revenue, and the Skouries mine starting in 2026 adds copper, another inflation-linked real asset. Gold output is guided to grow ~40% over three years, so higher metal prices land on rising volumes for strong operating leverage to a weaker real dollar.
key_risks: Skouries ramp-up delays/cost overruns; Greek and Turkish permitting risk.
notes: Price from 1 Sep 2026; a 18-Sep market cap of $10.5bn would imply ~$51 and P/Es ~20% higher. FY3 from Simply Wall St. Analyst count approximate.

name: Aris Mining
inflation_thesis: Almost pure, unhedged gold producer selling in USD with costs mostly in Colombian pesos, so an inflation-driven gold rally plus a weaker dollar widens margins sharply. The Segovia expansion and Marmato bulk-mining project lift output through 2027-28, so volume and price both drive earnings.
key_risks: Patchy execution (3 earnings misses in 4 quarters); Colombian security, artisanal-mining and permitting risk.
notes: FY0 revenue not found (FY1->FY3 revenue CAGR ~21%). One source shows much lower EPS that looks stale.

name: Ero Copper
inflation_thesis: Nearly all revenue is USD-priced copper while most costs are in Brazilian reais, so hot US inflation and a weaker dollar push up realised prices and margins. The Tucumã ramp-up adds volume on top, roughly doubling EPS from 2025 to 2026.
key_risks: BRL strength, Brazilian tax/permitting, and a history of back-loaded production guidance.
notes: TSX close C$48.37 (~US$35) on 10 Sep 2026 after an 8.5% drop. FY3 EPS derived from SWS net income; FY3 revenue extrapolated.

name: International Petroleum Corp
inflation_thesis: A pure USD-priced oil producer whose big Blackrod heavy-oil project is now built (first oil May 2026, 30,000 bopd plateau by late 2027), so capex is largely sunk and higher oil prices fall almost entirely to free cash flow and buybacks. Rising replacement costs for oil-sands projects also raise the value of an asset that is already built.
key_risks: Blackrod ramp-up execution, WCS heavy-oil differentials and a large Q2-26 EPS miss; expensive on 2026 earnings.
notes: Consensus in USD converted to CAD at 1.39. FY2/FY3 from Simply Wall St (Feb-26), set before the 2026 oil spike, so likely conservative. FY0 revenue estimated.

name: MMG Limited
sub_industry: Copper, zinc, cobalt (Las Bambas, Khoemacau, Kinsevere)
inflation_thesis: Large but under-followed copper/zinc/cobalt miner with USD-priced sales and high operating leverage to copper. H1-26 net income was already US$897m (vs ~US$0.4bn for all of 2025) and volumes grow with Khoemacau and Kinsevere, so consensus looks conservative.
key_risks: Las Bambas road blockades in Peru, DRC/Botswana risk, control by China Minmetals.
notes: EPS in HKD. H1-26 annualised EPS ~HK$1.13 vs FY26 consensus HK$1.00. Revenue consensus and analyst count not found.

name: Capstone Copper
sub_industry: Copper (Mantoverde, Mantos Blancos, Pinto Valley AZ)
inflation_thesis: Pure-play copper producer with USD-priced output and fast volume growth (Mantoverde, Mantos Blancos, Santo Domingo), so inflation-driven copper strength feeds straight into margins. Pinto Valley in Arizona gives US domestic-supply exposure.
key_risks: Chilean ramp-up execution; valuation is full if copper falls back.
notes: EPS converted from USD to CAD at 1.38 to match the CAD price. Consensus likely conservative (SWS from Mar-26; Seeking Alpha FY26 ~US$0.85).

name: Steel Dynamics
inflation_thesis: Low-cost US mini-mill steelmaker with its own scrap supply. In hot US inflation, domestic steel prices (tariff-protected by Section 232) rise faster than its scrap and energy costs; Q3-26 guidance of ~$5.36 EPS vs $2.74 a year ago shows margins already widening.
key_risks: Cyclical steel demand/pricing; aluminum mill ramp execution.
notes: Not under-the-radar (large cap). 2027-28 revenue from a model, not consensus.

name: Taseko Mines
inflation_thesis: Its Florence Copper mine in Arizona produces copper cathode inside the US, so it captures US tariff-driven COMEX premiums and reshoring demand on top of the copper price. Florence ramps from 30-35 Mlb (2026) toward ~85 Mlb a year on top of Gibraltar, giving one of the highest earnings leverages to copper of any producer.
key_risks: Florence ramp-up execution and Gibraltar grade variability; expensive on 2026 earnings and only ~3 analysts.
notes: EPS in CAD; price C$11.56 (US$8.38 on NYSE American). FY2 EPS is a two-broker average (Stifel 0.54, NBF 0.84).

name: Equinox Gold
inflation_thesis: Unhedged gold producer moving toward ~1 Moz/yr as Greenstone and Valentine reach full output, mostly in Canada with CAD costs, so a USD gold rally and weaker dollar widen margins. Most production is in safe North American jurisdictions.
key_risks: Greenstone/Valentine ramp-up risk; M&A dilution.
notes: FY0 revenue looks low (discontinued Brazil ops). Scotiabank FY27 EPS $1.75. 2028 revenue rests on one analyst. FY0 revenue left blank because the reported US$1.8bn excludes discontinued ops, which would overstate revenue growth.

name: Torex Gold Resources
inflation_thesis: Sells USD-priced gold plus copper and silver while most costs are in Mexican pesos, so inflation-driven metal prices flow straight into margins. Media Luna is ramping up and the EPO project and Prime Mining (Los Reyes) acquisition add volume, so price and production growth stack.
key_risks: Mexican security, mining-law and tax risk; Media Luna/EPO ramp-up execution.
notes: Consensus in CAD converted to USD at 1.38 (TSX price C$53.96). FY2028 EPS rests on one analyst; holding FY2 flat would give ~6.7x.

name: Aura Minerals
inflation_thesis: Fast-growing Latin American gold/copper producer selling in USD with costs in BRL, MXN and HNL, so USD inflation that lifts metal prices widens margins. New mines (Borborema, Era Dorada, MSG) drive ~20%+ annual revenue growth on top of price.
key_risks: Gold collar/derivative positions swing reported EPS; Latin American jurisdiction risk and leverage.
notes: FY0 statutory EPS negative due to derivative losses. Wide estimate spread (2026 EPS 5.55-10.08). H1-26 adjusted net income $201m.

name: Orezone Gold
inflation_thesis: Small, unhedged gold producer multiplying output via the Bombore hard-rock expansion and the Casa Berardi (Quebec) acquisition; record Q2-26 output of 58.6 koz at $4,401/oz. Very low valuation and high operating leverage make each USD gold move hit EPS hard.
key_risks: Burkina Faso sovereign/security risk; Casa Berardi integration and costs.
notes: Price C$3.23 converted at 1.38. EPS = SWS net income / 667m shares (Mar-26, 1-3 analysts). MarketScreener shows P/E 4.1x/2.7x. Price uncertain: Simply Wall St shows C$2.41 (would make P/Es ~25% lower); the higher C$3.23 is used to be conservative.

name: Westgold Resources
inflation_thesis: Sells unhedged USD-priced gold while costs are in AUD, so a falling USD in an inflationary regime is a double tailwind: higher US$ gold and a wider A$ margin. FY26 output hit a record 387 koz (NPAT +452%) and the three-year outlook targets 460-510 koz by FY29 with falling AISC.
key_risks: WA labour/cost inflation and execution on A$450-480m hub capex; history of operational misses.
notes: FY0 = underlying FY26 EPS. FY27/28 = SWS consensus earnings / ~987m shares; FY29 semi-extrapolated. Analyst count unconfirmed.

name: Catalyst Metals
inflation_thesis: Small, unhedged WA producer with AUD costs selling USD-priced gold, so it has high operating leverage to gold and to USD weakness. Its 10-year plan doubles output from ~100 koz to ~200 koz/yr (Trident, Old Highway, Cinnamon), with A$331m cash and no debt.
key_risks: Permitting/geology delays flagged in the Sep-26 guidance reset; small-cap execution.
notes: FY27 EPS is one broker (Morgans); TipRanks consensus A$0.84, SWS ~A$1.50. FY28/29 extrapolated conservatively. Later price snippets suggest A$5.6-5.9.

name: Panoro Energy
inflation_thesis: Pure Brent-linked oil producer selling USD cargoes from Gabon and Equatorial Guinea, with output growing from ~15k bopd to a guided 20k bopd in 2027, so higher nominal prices land on rising volumes. Tiny, under-followed and pays quarterly cash distributions.
key_risks: Lumpy cargo liftings, African PSC fiscal/political risk, thin and stale estimates.
notes: USD estimates converted to NOK at 10.5 on ~125m shares; most estimates pre-date the 2026 oil shock.

name: Ramelius Resources
inflation_thesis: Unhedged AUD-cost WA producer with a 74% EBITDA margin, so higher USD gold and a weaker USD lift A$ margins directly. Never Never reaches steady state in FY28 and the Mt Magnet mill expansion targets >500 koz/yr by FY30, making it one of the fastest growers with large net cash and a buyback.
key_risks: Execution/timing on Never Never and Mt Magnet; FY27 P/E still >12x until volumes arrive.
notes: FY0 revenue derived. FY27/28 = SWS earnings / ~1.88bn shares; Shaw has higher numbers. FY29 extrapolated. Price snippets range A$3.05-3.98; A$3.87 used.

name: Wesdome Gold Mines
inflation_thesis: Pure-play unhedged gold producer selling at USD gold prices with a Canadian-dollar cost base, so hot US inflation that lifts gold and weakens the USD widens margins; in 2025 revenue rose 64% and net income 2.5x. The Kiena ramp-up and better Eagle River grades add volume on top of price.
key_risks: Two narrow-vein underground mines (grade variability, concentration); 2028 consensus flat.
notes: Consensus in CAD converted to USD at 1.38 (TSX price C$33.43). Other snippets show C$26-33, so price timing uncertain.

name: Parex Resources
inflation_thesis: Almost entirely Brent-linked oil sold in USD, unhedged for 2026, with a mostly Colombian-peso cost base, so US inflation lifts revenue faster than costs. The Frontera E&P deal (closed 1 Jun 2026) roughly doubles output from ~45k to 82-91k boe/d, so EPS keeps growing into 2027-28 even if prices ease; ~6% dividend yield.
key_risks: Colombian political, tax and security risk; integrating Frontera assets that are larger than Parex itself.
notes: FY0 = 2025 EPS US$2.62 converted to CAD. EPS consensus in CAD (aktien.guide). Revenue estimates pre-date the Frontera deal and are too low; share count may have changed with the deal.

name: PRIO
sub_industry: Offshore oil E&P (Frade, Peregrino, Albacora Leste, Wahoo)
inflation_thesis: Almost pure Brent-linked oil exporter with USD revenue, a large BRL cost base and a lifting cost of only ~$12.5/bbl, giving very high operating leverage to higher nominal oil and a weaker dollar. Output steps up from 106 kbpd (2025) to ~187 kbpd (2026) and ~204 kbpd (2027) with Peregrino and Wahoo, so EPS roughly quadruples from 2025 even at flat oil.
key_risks: Brent volatility, Wahoo/Peregrino execution and IBAMA licensing, Brazilian export-levy/tax changes.
notes: Reports in USD; EPS converted to BRL (MarketScreener consensus net income / ~860m shares). MarketScreener 2026 P/E 5.9x matches. Analyst count approximate.

name: Hochschild Mining
sub_industry: Silver & gold (Peru, Argentina, Brazil Mara Rosa)
inflation_thesis: Silver and gold are the classic US-inflation and weak-dollar hedges, and its costs are mostly in Peruvian soles, Argentine pesos and reais, so each extra dollar of metal price goes almost straight to margin. Mara Rosa and Inmaculada operating leverage takes EPS from $0.31 to ~$0.79.
key_risks: Peru political/permitting/community risk, Mara Rosa ramp-up, Argentine FX and export controls.
notes: LSE price 560p converted to USD at 1.33. EPS treated as USD (reporting currency); if it is GBP the P/Es are ~25% lower. FY0 is pre-exceptional.

name: GeoPark
inflation_thesis: Pure upstream oil producer with Brent-linked USD revenue against field, labour and service costs in Colombian and Argentine pesos, so it is highly geared to nominal oil prices. New Vaca Muerta blocks ramp volumes in 2027-28, lifting consensus revenue ~70% from 2025 to 2028.
key_risks: Heavy Vaca Muerta capex and debt during the ramp, mature Llanos 34 decline, Colombian fiscal risk; only 1-3 analysts.
notes: 2026-27 consensus (2-3 analysts; company guides $0.87/$1.38). 2028 set to a conservative $2.06 extrapolation instead of the single $4.47 estimate. Price from 1 Aug 2026.

name: Gulf Marine Services
inflation_thesis: Liftboat owner with USD contracts from Gulf national oil companies; with no newbuilds and rising replacement costs, dayrates step up at each renewal, and high oil prices support Gulf offshore spending. Rapid deleveraging shifts value from debt to equity.
key_risks: 2026 Gulf/Iran conflict disrupted operations (H1-26 loss incl. impairment); only 2 analysts; estimates pre-date H1.
notes: USD net income estimates (Jul-26) converted to pence on ~1.08bn shares.

name: Pampa Energía
inflation_thesis: Mostly dollarised revenue (USD-indexed power contracts, USD gas, fast-growing exportable shale oil from Rincón de Aranda) against peso labour and services; record Q2-26 oil & gas EBITDA of $415m drives a ~25% EPS CAGR.
key_risks: Argentine macro/FX/regulatory risk (tariffs, gas price caps); thin coverage, noisy estimates.
notes: Per ADR (25 shares). vcpscanner's own model is lower (8.72/9.90/10.40).

name: Ternium
inflation_thesis: Its Mexican flat-steel prices track tariff-protected US Midwest hot-rolled coil import parity, so US steel inflation feeds straight into USD pricing while much of its cost base is in pesos and reais. The Pesquería mill ramp-up and USMCA nearshoring take EPS from $2.17 to ~$6.7.
key_risks: US Section 232/USMCA review hitting Mexican steel; Chinese oversupply; stronger peso.
notes: FactSet median (11 analysts); another consensus has 2026 EPS $3.94. Price uncertain (a quoted forward P/E implies ~$46). Price set to ~$46 (July close $44.84; Sept range $44.7-46.5); the $58 quote looked wrong.

name: Navios Maritime Partners
inflation_thesis: Owns ~180 vessels across containers, dry bulk and tankers whose replacement cost rises with steel and shipyard inflation, yet the units trade far below NAV. $4.4bn of USD contracted backlog runs to 2037 while uncontracted ships reprice to nominal freight rates, and newbuild deliveries keep EPS growing into 2027-28 — rare in shipping.
key_risks: Complex MLP controlled by its sponsor (Angeliki Frangou); dry-bulk/tanker spot exposure if the cycle turns.
notes: 2027-28 EPS from a single alternative source (indicative). Revenue 2026-28 partly model-based. Avg target $98 (4 analysts).

name: Minerva Foods
inflation_thesis: South America's largest beef exporter sells in USD while buying cattle and paying labour in local currencies; record US beef prices (US herd shortage) and US food inflation widen the export spread.
key_risks: High leverage (~2.6-3x net debt/EBITDA); cattle cycle; China/US trade measures.
notes: 2026-27 EPS are JPMorgan's (single broker); 2028 SWS consensus; revenue derived from growth rate. Stock -36% YTD.

name: Suzano
inflation_thesis: World's largest, lowest-cost market-pulp exporter: almost all revenue is USD-priced pulp while wood, labour and costs are in reais, so US inflation and a weaker dollar widen margins. The Cerrado mill ramp-up and deleveraging take core EPS from $1.26 (2026) to $1.89 (2028).
key_risks: Pulp price cycle (China demand, new capacity), BRL strength, high net debt.
notes: 2025 EPS inflated by non-cash FX gains, so FY0 left blank and growth measured 2026-28. FactSet median lower (1.20/1.39/1.56). Well covered.

name: Brava Energia
inflation_thesis: ~80% of output is Brent-priced oil sold in USD while costs are in BRL, so hotter US inflation and a weaker dollar widen margins. Volumes grow from 81 kboe/d (2025) to ~100 kboe/d in 2027 as Papa-Terra phase 2 and new Atlanta wells come on, so EPS peaks in 2027 rather than 2026.
key_risks: Ecopetrol now owns 51% after a partial tender at R$23 (minority/free-float risk); ~2.2x leverage; offshore delays.
notes: EPS = SWS consensus net income / ~466m shares. FY0 not found.

name: PT Timah
inflation_thesis: World #2 listed tin miner selling LME tin in USD (~US$55,700/t, +36% YTD) against rupiah costs, so price plus a weak rupiah gives huge operating leverage. A government crackdown on illegal mining is returning ore and market share, so volumes rise too.
key_risks: Tin-price correction; Indonesian royalty hikes; SOE governance history.
notes: EPS = average of 3 broker net-profit estimates / 7.45bn shares; 2028 extrapolated (+8%).

name: Lingbao Gold Group
sub_industry: Gold mining & smelting (+ control of St Barbara / Simberi)
inflation_thesis: Small, under-followed gold producer with RMB and PNG-kina costs and USD-linked gold revenue, giving high leverage to gold. Taking control of St Barbara (Simberi, PNG) in April 2026 adds a big production step-up; 2025 profit already rose 122%.
key_risks: Smelting/refining dilutes gold beta; PNG integration; convertible-bond fair-value losses.
notes: RMB converted to HKD at 1.087. 2027 from consensus net profit / ~1.29bn shares; 2028 extrapolated (+8%).

name: Alamtri Minerals Indonesia
inflation_thesis: Sells coking coal and, from 2H26, aluminium from a new 500ktpa smelter — both USD-priced hard commodities that track US industrial inflation — while labour, services and hydro power costs are in rupiah. The smelter ramp gives real volume growth (revenue tripling 2025-28), so EPS growth doesn't depend on the coal cycle.
key_risks: Smelter ramp-up delays/losses (US$45.5m 1H26 loss); coking-coal weakness; parent-group governance.
notes: USD broker net-profit forecasts converted at 16,300 on 40.88bn shares; a second broker is higher. 16 of 17 analysts Buy; target Rp2,313.

name: Zijin Gold International
inflation_thesis: Pure-play gold producer spun out of Zijin Mining, with output growing from 46.9t (2025) to ~59t guided in 2026 and more through 2028 at an AISC of ~US$1,500/oz, so margins widen sharply when inflation lifts gold. Most costs are in emerging-market currencies (Central Asia, Africa, South America, PNG) that tend to weaken against the dollar.
key_risks: Large cap and well covered; emerging-market resource-nationalism risk; July-2026 profit warning and broker estimates below consensus.
notes: Latest quotes ~HK$204-209 (market cap ~HK$563bn); earlier HK$127 quote was stale. Broker numbers (Guosen, BofA) are lower than this consensus.

name: Medco Energi Internasional
sub_industry: Oil & gas E&P + Amman Mineral (copper/gold) stake
inflation_thesis: Sells USD-priced oil and oil-linked gas at a cash cost of only ~$8.6/boe from a USD asset base, plus copper/gold exposure via its Amman Mineral stake. H1-26 net profit of $275m (+650% y/y) shows the leverage to higher dollar commodity prices.
key_risks: Net debt/EBITDA ~2x; Amman Mineral smelter/export permits; Indonesian PSC terms.
notes: Single-broker (BRIDS) USD EPS converted to IDR at 16,700. FY25 EPS depressed by impairments (low base). FY26 likely conservative vs H1 actual.

name: Oil India
inflation_thesis: Sells crude and gas at USD-linked prices while costs are mostly in rupees, so higher US inflation and dollar oil prices flow straight to margins (Q1 FY27 EPS +253% y/y). The Numaligarh refinery expansion from 3 to 9 MTPA (start ~Mar-27) adds a volume-driven growth step in FY28.
key_risks: Government windfall taxes/subsidy sharing; NRL commissioning delays; crude reversal.
notes: Sharpely median consensus; FY0 derived from growth rates; FY29 extrapolated (+7%).

name: China Gold International Resources
sub_industry: Gold & copper (Jiama, Tibet; CSH, Inner Mongolia)
inflation_thesis: Sells USD-priced gold and copper against an RMB cost base, so a weaker dollar and rising nominal metal prices go almost entirely to margin. The Jiama restart and 'three-step' expansion add volume on top of price; net cash and a record dividend.
key_risks: Single-asset Tibet operating/safety risk (Jiama suspended 2023-24); parent China National Gold controls capital allocation.
notes: Consensus (4 analysts) looks stale: H1-26 EPS was already ~HK$10. Latest quotes HK$260-273 (stock has roughly doubled since June), so P/Es use HK$260.4; FY3 extrapolated.

name: Indo Tambangraya Megah
inflation_thesis: Pure USD thermal-coal exporter (Newcastle-linked prices, sold across Asia) with rupiah costs, net cash and a high-payout dividend. Sales volumes are guided up ~10% in 2026 from new concessions, so energy-led inflation in seaborne coal prices lands on rising volumes while the weak rupiah holds costs down.
key_risks: Indonesian RKAB quota cuts, higher DMO share at capped prices and royalty hikes; wide broker dispersion (a bearish broker sees flat profit).
notes: Price implied from KB Valbury target/upside (31 Aug). FY27 EPS from one bullish broker (Ajaib); FY28 extrapolated +5%.

name: Jiangxi Copper (H)
inflation_thesis: China's largest copper producer (Dexing mine, smelting, stake in First Quantum) selling USD-priced copper, gold, silver and acid against RMB costs, so higher nominal metal prices lift mining profit and by-product/inventory gains; H1-26 profit guided up to +103%. The H-shares trade at a deep discount to the A-shares.
key_risks: Mostly smelting purchased concentrate, where record-low treatment charges cap margins; low self-sufficiency (~15-20%); hedging losses.
notes: RMB EPS converted to HKD at 1.087; 2027-28 from SWS consensus net profit (8 analysts). Market cap covers A+H at the H price.

name: Trimegah Bangun Persada (Harita Nickel)
inflation_thesis: Low-cost integrated Indonesian nickel producer (saprolite ore, NPI and HPAL nickel sulphate) whose USD-priced output is made with rupiah labour and captive power, so a weak rupiah and higher metal prices widen margins. KPS Phase 3 and HPAL ramp-ups add volume through 2028; ~4.5x FY2 P/E with a Rp1tn buyback.
key_risks: Structural nickel oversupply (price upside depends on RKAB quota cuts); HPAL tailings/ESG scrutiny; controlling-shareholder selldowns.
notes: Consensus as quoted by BRI Danareksa (Aug-26); FY0 derived from dividend/payout; 2028 revenue extrapolated.

name: Corporación América Airports
sub_industry: Airport concessions (Argentina, Italy, Brazil, Uruguay, Ecuador, Armenia)
inflation_thesis: Reports in USD, and international passenger fees in Argentina, Uruguay, Ecuador and Armenia are USD-denominated with regulated tariffs that preserve real USD returns. Debt is low (0.7x EBITDA) and mostly fixed-rate, so nominal fee increases flow straight to EBITDA while traffic grows ~10% a year.
key_risks: Argentine macro/FX/regulatory risk (concessions, tariffs, hyperinflation accounting noise); Q2-26 cost pressure and a 35% EPS miss.
notes: FY0 = reported basic EPS (2025 consensus had been $1.51, so growth partly reflects basis). 2027 revenue interpolated. Price from late August.

name: Granite Ridge Resources
sub_industry: Non-operated oil & gas interests (Permian, Eagle Ford, Bakken, Haynesville)
inflation_thesis: Holds non-operated interests across major US basins (~51% oil), so higher oil prices pass straight to revenue (Q2-26 revenue +37% y/y, mostly price). Management targets 8-10% production growth in 2027 and a free-cash-flow inflection after 2026, stacking volume and price leverage at ~7x 2027 earnings.
key_risks: As a non-op owner it pays its share of capex and opex, so cost inflation partly offsets price gains; only 2 analysts.
notes: Adjusted EPS basis. 2027 EPS is a single broker (Northland); 2028 extrapolated (+8%).

name: ASUR (Grupo Aeroportuario del Sureste)
inflation_thesis: Cancún traffic is mostly international passengers paying a USD-denominated fee, Mexican maximum tariffs are inflation-indexed, and San Juan (Puerto Rico) earns USD directly. Costs are mostly fixed and the balance sheet is net cash, so US inflation and a strong dollar pass almost entirely to EBITDA.
key_risks: Weaker Cancún international traffic (US demand, hurricanes, sargassum, new Tulum airport) and Mexican regulatory risk.
notes: FactSet median of 15 analysts (per ADR, USD). FY0 = trailing-12-month EPS proxy ($19.20). Stock -23% YTD.

name: Boise Cascade
inflation_thesis: All-US plywood/engineered-wood maker and the largest US building-materials distributor, so lumber, panel and construction-cost inflation flows straight into its prices and revalues its inventory. Duties and tariffs on Canadian lumber lift US wood prices without touching its cost base; net cash.
key_risks: Delayed housing recovery (high mortgage rates) keeps panel pricing soft and pushes out the 2027-28 rebound.
notes: 2027 EPS interpolated between 2026 consensus and 2028 TickFlow consensus ($8.20, range 7.30-9.10). Q2-26 beat ($1.63 vs $1.23).

name: Grupo Aeroportuario del Pacífico (GAP)
inflation_thesis: Tariffs reset in real terms under its 2025-29 plan and indexed to Mexican PPI; international passengers (Los Cabos, Puerto Vallarta, Guadalajara) pay USD fees and its Jamaican airports bill in USD. Big tariff step-ups on a fixed base drive ~15% EPS growth; stock is near its 52-week low.
key_risks: Heavy capex and leverage; peso rebound; Mexican political pressure on fees.
notes: MXN EPS per ADR converted at 18.5; 2028 revenue extrapolated.

name: Triple Flag Precious Metals
inflation_thesis: Revenue is attributable gold/silver ounces times the USD spot price, with fixed per-ounce stream payments and cost-free royalties, so ~93% asset margins mean almost all of an inflation-driven precious-metals move reaches EPS. Guided volume growth from ~100k to 140-150k GEOs by 2030 adds to price leverage.
key_risks: Gold has pulled back from its Jan-2026 high; 2026 GEO guidance below 2025; EPS flattens in 2028; ~19x FY2 is not cheap.
notes: FY0 = 2025 adjusted EPS. FY26 estimates range $1.08-1.45.

name: OMA (Grupo Aeroportuario del Centro Norte)
inflation_thesis: Maximum tariffs are set in real terms and indexed to Mexican inflation, and the passenger fee for international travellers is set in USD, so revenue rises with both inflation and the dollar. The new 2026-30 development programme lifts tariffs on a largely sunk asset base, widening a ~74% EBITDA margin; nearshoring in Monterrey drives traffic.
key_risks: Political/regulatory intervention in Mexican airport fees; peso strength; airline fleet groundings.
notes: MXN consensus per ADR converted at 18.5. FY0 estimated from TTM (~$6.07/ADR).

name: DNO ASA
sub_industry: Oil & gas E&P (North Sea, Kurdistan, West Africa)
inflation_thesis: After buying Sval it is mainly a North Sea producer (~85k boe/d) selling Brent oil and European gas in USD against NOK costs; Q2-26 revenue hit a record US$761m. Shut-in Kurdistan barrels are free upside on restart, and its reserves gain value as replacement costs rise.
key_risks: 78% Norwegian tax rate dampens upside; Kurdistan security/payments; bond debt.
notes: USD EPS converted to NOK at 10.5; 2027-28 EPS = consensus net income / ~975m shares. Price derived from target upside (approx). ~8.5% dividend yield. Promoted from bench in round 5.

name: Atalaya Mining Copper
inflation_thesis: Almost pure, net-cash copper producer selling a USD-priced hard asset that benefits from US inflation and US/EU grid and reshoring demand. Growth projects (San Dionisio, Masa Valverde, Touro) lift output without much dilution; H1-26 EPS was already EUR0.554, so consensus looks conservative.
key_risks: Single main mine; Spanish permitting for expansions; EUR cost base.
notes: EUR EPS converted to GBP at 0.872. Consensus likely stale: H1-26 annualises to ~EUR1.1 EPS; MarketScreener shows 9.1x 2026 / 6.9x 2027. Promoted from bench in round 5.

name: Tidewater
sub_industry: Offshore supply vessels (world's largest OSV fleet)
inflation_thesis: World's largest offshore supply-vessel owner, with USD dayrates that reprice every 1-3 years. The newbuild orderbook is near zero and replacement cost is far above secondhand values, so steel, yard and crew inflation raise the dayrate any new vessel needs and the existing fleet captures it. High 2026 oil prices support offshore spending, and repricing shows in EPS tripling from 2026 to 2028.
key_risks: Offshore capex deferral if oil falls; not cheap on 2026-27 earnings; widely covered.
notes: FY0 uses underlying 2025 EPS (~$2.6); reported $6.64 included a $201.5m one-off tax benefit. Second source: 2027/28 EPS $5.81/$7.91. Promoted from bench in round 5.

name: Asia-Potash International
inflation_thesis: Pure-play potash producer selling at USD world benchmark prices from a very low-cost Laos mine (cheap labour and power). US food inflation lifts grain prices, farm incomes and potash demand, while its 2nd-4th million-tonne lines ramp up — so EPS keeps growing strongly into 2027-28.
key_risks: Laos mine ramp-up/flooding execution risk; potash price reversal (China contract, Belarus/Russia supply).
notes: Average of China Merchants and Western Securities estimates (Jul/Aug-26). H1-26 net profit +58%. Price date approximate (Sep 7 close was 45.58).

name: Tharisa
inflation_thesis: Sells PGMs and chrome in USD against mostly rand costs, so higher dollar metal prices from US inflation and a weaker dollar widen margins. Volume growth comes from Karo Platinum in Zimbabwe (~400koz/yr PGMs, commissioning 2027), reflected in a 25% FY28 revenue step-up.
key_risks: Karo financing/ramp-up in Zimbabwe; chrome price swings; only 2 analysts.
notes: Price 125p converted at 1.33. FY28 EPS extrapolated from the FY28 revenue step-up. FY25 EPS may include one-offs.

name: Sibanye-Stillwater (ADR)
inflation_thesis: Has the highest operating leverage of the South African miners: high-cost rand-based gold and PGM shafts selling USD-priced gold, platinum, palladium and rhodium, so higher dollar metal prices add margin far faster than revenue. 2026 was hit by a gold strike and Montana flooding, so 2027 is a volume-recovery year on top of higher prices.
key_risks: Operational fragility (strikes, flooding), possible Stillwater closure, high gearing; 2028 EPS dips.
notes: Per ADR (4 shares). EPS derived from SWS consensus net profit; no reliable 2026 figure (H1 loss). Widely covered.

name: Pan African Resources
sub_industry: Gold (Barberton, Evander, Mogale tailings; Tennant Creek)
inflation_thesis: Unhedged gold producer with a South African rand cost base, so dollar gold gains from US inflation go almost straight to margin (FY26 received price $4,235/oz, +55%). Gold sold rose 38% in FY26 from the Mogale tailings ramp-up and Tennant Creek, and earnings are forecast to keep rising into FY28.
key_risks: Share-price data inconsistent; SA power/operational issues; rand strength; Tennant Creek execution.
notes: EPS derived from SWS consensus net income / ~2.06bn shares; FY29 extrapolated. Price 136.3p (x1.33) is uncertain — another source shows 92.65p.

name: Sylvania Platinum
inflation_thesis: Reports in USD and sells PGMs and chrome at USD prices from a low-cost, almost entirely rand-based tailings-retreatment operation, so nearly all USD price gains reach the bottom line (FY26 revenue more than doubled). The Thaba JV adds a first full year in FY27; debt-free with net cash ~20% of market cap.
key_risks: PGM prices have reset lower (Edison cut FY27 EPS 57%); modest volume growth; thin, mostly sponsored coverage.
notes: Edison estimates (Sep-26); FY28 from an earlier Edison iteration; FY29 extrapolated. Price 95p x1.33.

name: New Hope Corp
inflation_thesis: Sells USD-priced seaborne high-energy thermal coal from an Australian-dollar cost base, so energy-led inflation lifts realisations directly. Volumes grow as New Acland Stage 3 ramps (FY27 guidance ~12.7Mt, +10%), lowering unit costs, and EPS rebounds sharply from a depressed FY26; strong balance sheet and fully franked dividends.
key_risks: Thermal coal prices; Bell Potter (Sell) and Macquarie downgrades after the run to a 52-week high.
notes: FY ends July. FY29 EPS extrapolated flat; FY28 revenue from SWS narrative.

name: Sinofert Holdings
inflation_thesis: Sinochem's fertilizer arm and China's largest potash importer/distributor, with its own phosphate and compound-fertilizer plants; higher USD fertilizer prices lift revenue and inventory gains. Deep value at ~4x earnings with a net-cash-leaning balance sheet.
key_risks: Mostly distribution with thin margins; consensus (2 analysts) looks optimistic vs H1-26 profit +6.7%.
notes: RMB converted to HKD at 1.095; 2027 EPS backed out of a quoted P/E; 2028 extrapolated (+4%).

name: Guizhou Chanhen Chemical
inflation_thesis: Owns captive phosphate rock in Guizhou and Guangxi with new mines and downstream capacity coming on stream; rock and phosphate product prices follow USD fertilizer and food prices while mining costs are fixed, so food/energy inflation widens margins on rising volumes.
key_risks: H1-26 profit only +4.5% (consensus may be cut); Chinese phosphate export quotas cap price pass-through.
notes: Consensus of 14 institutions (Jun-26). Revenue from one broker. Price derived from market cap (Aug-23).

name: Yunnan Yuntianhua
inflation_thesis: China's largest phosphate-fertilizer maker with big captive phosphate-rock reserves and coal-based urea; product prices follow USD DAP/urea benchmarks while rock costs are internal, so grain and energy inflation widens spreads. Cheap (~9x) with a ~50% payout.
key_risks: Sulfur cost spikes; Chinese export quotas on DAP/MAP; EPS growth only ~6%/yr.
notes: Average of two brokers; revenue from one broker. Price from 20 Aug.

name: Alliance Resource Partners
inflation_thesis: Sells USD-priced thermal coal to US utilities whose plant retirements are being delayed by data-centre load growth, supporting contract volumes and repricing; its oil & gas mineral royalties capture commodity inflation with almost no costs, and the high-payout LP passes cash to holders.
key_risks: Plant retirements/gas-to-coal switching; labour and supply inflation on fixed-price contracts.
notes: 2027 = avg of Sidoti/Noble; 2028 extrapolated (+5%). ~9.4x FY2 but only ~8% EPS CAGR.

name: Archer
inflation_thesis: Asset-light platform-drilling and well-services contractor earning USD from North Sea operator contracts with cost-indexation clauses and from Argentina (Vaca Muerta) and Brazil. High oil prices keep platform drilling and well intervention busy; backlog rose to $3.9bn and Q2-26 EBITDA margin hit a record 17.1%, so rising day-rates and indexation flow into a very low-multiple equity.
key_risks: Very thin coverage, leveraged balance sheet, negative trailing EPS, Argentina macro/FX risk.
notes: 2026-27 EPS implied from MarketScreener P/Es; 2028 extrapolated from a single analyst. Sources conflict (MarketScreener net income would give ~NOK 3.6/4.2). Price ~NOK 24.8-25.5; ~10% dividend yield; avg target NOK 35.5.

name: Anton Oilfield Services
inflation_thesis: Most revenue comes from USD-denominated oilfield-management and service contracts in Iraq, Africa and Central Asia that reprice with oil prices and US inflation, while its Chinese engineering cost base stays cheap. High oil prices push national oil companies to outsource production enhancement; a growing order book supports a 2027-28 recovery at ~4x earnings.
key_risks: Middle East war hit Iraq operations (H1-26 profit -37% with a large FX loss), so 2026 consensus is likely too high.
notes: Consensus likely stale (pre-H1); 2028 extrapolated (+15%). Price HK$0.77-0.83.

name: Seadrill
inflation_thesis: Pure deepwater driller with 7th-gen drillships rolling onto new contracts in 2026-27 as leading-edge rates reach $450-500k/day; no newbuilds, so USD dayrates reprice for inflation.
key_risks: Brazil (Petrobras) renewals and idle time between contracts could delay the 2027 step-up; very wide estimate dispersion; ~14x 2027.
notes: 2026 consensus may be stale (Q2 beat and guidance raised). 2028 extrapolated flat (vcpscanner model 2.82).

name: Deep Industries
sub_industry: Gas compression, workover rigs, offshore barges
inflation_thesis: Rupee-cost oilfield services with a ~₹3,000cr order book (ONGC, private E&Ps) moving into offshore barges and production-enhancement contracts whose dayrates are benchmarked to USD global rig/vessel rates; Q1 FY27 profit +45%.
key_risks: ONGC tender dependence; offshore execution; thin coverage.
notes: FY29 EPS extrapolated (+15%); management guides FY27 PAT ₹400cr+ (~₹62 EPS) — upside to consensus.

name: Ranger Energy Services
inflation_thesis: Sells workover-rig hours and wireline work at short-cycle USD rates that can be repriced against wage, steel and fuel inflation within a quarter; work is mostly production maintenance and well plugging, which high oil prices make worthwhile. The American Well Services deal (bought at <2.5x EBITDA) adds Permian rigs whose replacement cost is far above the price paid.
key_risks: Small cap with recent EPS misses; workover demand falls if oil drops.
notes: WallStreetZen consensus; FY0 backed out from stated growth; 2028 revenue extrapolated.

name: National Energy Services Reunited
inflation_thesis: MENA oilfield-services provider whose contracts are in USD or USD-pegged currencies with Gulf national oil companies and reprice for cost inflation under long-term frameworks; high oil prices raise capex, and Aramco's Jafurah unconventional-gas contract is ramping (Q2-26 revenue +59%, 2026 guidance raised to $2bn+).
key_risks: Aramco/Jafurah concentration; stock already re-rated ~287% in a year; past accounting/governance issues.
notes: 2026 consensus ($1.71) looks low vs Q1+Q2 actual + Q3/Q4 estimates ($1.88). 2028 extrapolated (+15%).

name: Elnusa
sub_industry: Oilfield services (seismic, drilling, well services) + fuel distribution
inflation_thesis: Pertamina's main oilfield-services arm: 2026's high oil prices and Indonesia's production push lift drilling, seismic and well-service volumes, and fuel-distribution revenue rises with oil prices. Rupiah costs mean a weak IDR and strong dollar oil widen margins; ~5x 2027 earnings.
key_risks: Dependence on Pertamina capex and budgets; regulated/negotiated pricing.
notes: Only 2026 consensus found; 2027-28 extrapolated (~10%/yr). H1-26 profit +29%. Price from Aug.

name: Enerflex
inflation_thesis: Runs a US contract-compression fleet and long-term energy-infrastructure contracts that typically carry CPI/cost escalators, while sharply rising new-compressor costs support higher rents on the existing fleet. Engineered-systems backlog is cost-plus, it reports in USD, and it's expanding for Permian gas, LNG feedgas and gas-for-power demand.
key_risks: Latin American/Middle East contract and country risk; volatile reported EPS from one-offs.
notes: FY0 = normalised 2025 EPS (~$1.18; reported $0.51 incl. refinancing loss). 2027-28 from TickFlow quarterly sums; CAD consensus converts to slightly higher figures.

name: Vallourec
inflation_thesis: Owns scarce premium seamless pipe mills; its US mills (Vallourec Star), Brazil and Middle East OCTG contracts are priced in USD with index-linked or annually reset pricing. US inflation and tariffs raise imported-pipe prices, lifting domestic OCTG prices and margins, while high oil prices drive well counts — consensus sees EBITDA rising from ~€786m (2026) to €1.08bn (2028).
key_risks: OCTG price cycles and US rig counts; Middle East logistics disruption hurt 2026 volumes.
notes: Per-share consensus (9-10 analysts). Price after a €2.05 interim dividend; exact date unverified.

name: Natural Gas Services Group
inflation_thesis: Pure-play gas-compression rental company: monthly rates on large-horsepower units reprice as contracts renew, and sharply higher new-compressor costs support rates and returns on the existing fleet. Utilisation is at a record, 2026 EBITDA guidance was raised despite cost inflation, and the Flatrock acquisition adds Permian gas demand.
key_risks: Debt-funded fleet growth (Flatrock ~$110m cash); customer concentration.
notes: 2026 consensus pre-dates Flatrock and guidance raise (likely low). 2027 from TickFlow quarterly sums; 2028 extrapolated (+12%).
